`run-server` stays in the foreground; Ctrl-C / SIGTERM stops the container.

## Client

```sh
# Upload every file under ./photos that the server does not have yet, or
# has with different content (compared by SHA-256). Identical files are not
# re-sent; blobs that exist only on the server are left alone.
./run-client push ./photos --server http://127.0.0.1:8080
#   uploaded 2024/trip/IMG_0001.jpg (new, 3182044 bytes)
#   uploaded notes.txt (changed, 412 bytes)
#   push done: 2 uploaded, 57 unchanged, 59 file(s) scanned

# The mirror image: download every blob that is missing under ./photos or
# differs from the local file (by SHA-256) to ./photos/<key>, creating
# directories as needed. Identical files are not re-downloaded; local files
# the server does not have are left alone.
./run-client pull ./photos --server http://127.0.0.1:8080
#   downloaded 2024/trip/IMG_0002.jpg (new, 2960113 bytes)
#   downloaded notes.txt (changed, 440 bytes)
#   pull done: 2 downloaded, 58 unchanged, 60 blob(s) listed

# Dry run: compare ./photos with the server and print what push and pull
# would do — one line per differing key, grouped by direction, then a
# summary. Nothing is changed on either side; exit code 0 means the
# comparison succeeded, whether or not there are differences.
./run-client status ./photos --server http://127.0.0.1:8080
#   upload    2024/trip/IMG_0003.jpg  (missing on server, 2871200 bytes)
#   download  2024/trip/IMG_0002.jpg  (missing locally, 2960113 bytes)
#   differs   notes.txt  (local 440 bytes, server 412 bytes; push would upload, pull would download)
#   status: 1 to upload, 1 to download, 1 differs on both sides, 58 unchanged (dry run: nothing was changed)
./run-client status ./photos --server http://127.0.0.1:8080       # when everything matches:
#   status: in sync, 61 file(s) identical on both sides (dry run: nothing was changed)

# Both ways in one pass: files only here go up, blobs only there come down,
# a file changed on one side since the last sync is copied to the other, and
# a file changed on both sides goes to the fresher mtime / modified_at
# (local wins a tie). Nothing is ever deleted on either side.
./run-client sync ./photos --server http://127.0.0.1:8080
#   uploaded 2024/trip/IMG_0003.jpg (new, 2871200 bytes)
#   downloaded 2024/trip/IMG_0002.jpg (new, 2960113 bytes)
#   uploaded notes.txt (changed locally, 440 bytes)
#   downloaded todo.md (conflict, server is newer, 1024 bytes)
#   sync done: 2 uploaded, 2 downloaded, 58 unchanged, 1 conflict(s) resolved

SYNCBOX_SERVER=http://127.0.0.1:8080 ./run-client pull ./photos   # env instead of --server
```

`run-client <push|pull|sync|status> <dir> --server <url>` forwards the
subcommand and arguments to the `syncbox` executable (`bin/syncbox`) running
in a container; `--server` falls back to `SYNCBOX_SERVER`.

`push` walks `<dir>` recursively; a file's key is its POSIX path relative to
`<dir>` (`docs/readme.txt`), exactly the server's key convention, and is sent
percent-encoded so names with spaces or non-ASCII characters round-trip
byte for byte. Hidden files are included. Symbolic links (to files or
directories) and special files (sockets, FIFOs, devices) cannot be blobs and
are skipped with a warning on stderr — links are never followed. The server
listing (`GET /blobs`) is fetched once; each local file whose key is missing
there or whose `sha256` differs is streamed with `PUT /blobs/{key}`, and the
`sha256` the server reports back is checked against the local one. Progress
goes to stdout (one line per uploaded file plus a summary), warnings and
errors to stderr.

`pull` fetches the listing once and compares each blob's `sha256` with the
file at `<dir>/<key>`: a blob with no local file, or whose hash differs, is
fetched with `GET /blobs/{key}`; one with an identical local file is skipped
without a request. Each download is streamed into a staging file
(`.syncbox-tmp-<16 hex digits>`) in the target's directory, hashed on the
way, flushed to disk and `rename(2)`d onto `<dir>/<key>` only if the hash
matches the listing — so a file under `<dir>` is either untouched or
complete, never half-written, and a blob replaced on the server during the
pull (or a corrupted transfer) is reported instead of installed. Replacing a
file keeps its permission bits; a new file gets the default ones. Missing
parent directories are created. Staging files are removed on every outcome,
including an interrupted run (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM); only a hard kill can leave
one behind. Keys from the listing are not trusted: an absolute key, one with
`.` or `..` segments, empty segments or NUL bytes is refused, and a key is
never resolved through a symlink — a symlinked directory on the way, or a
directory, symlink or special file at the target itself, is reported as "in
the way" and nothing is written, mirroring `push`, which never follows links
either. Local files and directories the server does not list are never
deleted or modified; `pull` only adds and replaces.

`status` is the dry run of both: it scans `<dir>` like `push`, fetches the
listing once like `pull`, and compares the two by key and `sha256`. Every key
falls into exactly one group — `upload` (only local; `push` would upload it),
`download` (only on the server; `pull` would download it), `differs` (on both
sides with different content; `push` would upload the local version, `pull`
would download the server's — which one `sync` picks is decided by its
conflict rule, and `status` does not guess) or unchanged (identical, only
counted). Lines are grouped in that order and sorted by key, followed by a
summary line; an identical tree prints just the `in sync` summary. The
command never changes anything: no file under `<dir>` is created, modified
or removed, and the only request it sends is `GET /blobs` — the listing
already carries every hash the comparison needs, so not even `GET
/blobs/{key}` is issued, let alone `PUT` or `DELETE`. A download that `pull`
would refuse (a directory or symlink where the file would go, a key that
could leave the directory) is still listed as a download, with a `pull would
fail: …` note. The exit code is `0` whenever the comparison succeeded,
regardless of how many differences there are.

`sync` is `push` and `pull` in one pass plus the spec's conflict rule. It
scans `<dir>`, fetches the listing once and walks the union of keys. A key
present on one side only is copied to the other (`uploaded … (new, …)` /
`downloaded … (new, …)`); a key identical on both sides is left alone. When
the hashes differ, the *last known common state* decides whose change it is:
`sync` records, in `<dir>/.syncbox/state.json`, the SHA-256 of every key
that was identical on both sides at the end of a run. On the next run a side
whose hash still equals that recorded value has not changed, so the
difference belongs to the other side alone and is copied in that direction
(`changed locally` → upload, `changed on server` → download) — timestamps
play no role in these cases. Only when *both* sides have moved away from the
common version is it a conflict, resolved exactly as the spec says: the
fresher of the server's `modified_at` (the time the blob was stored, from
`GET /blobs`) and the local file's mtime wins, and on a tie the local version
wins (`conflict, server is newer` / `conflict, local is newer` /
`conflict, same mtime, local wins`). The two instants are compared exactly;
since `modified_at` has millisecond precision, a local mtime inside the same
millisecond but after it counts as newer, which gives the same answer as the
tie rule. Content is compared by hash only — a file touched but not changed
is unchanged. When no common version is known yet (the first run on a
directory, or a key never seen in sync before) and the two sides differ, the
same mtime rule picks the side to copy, reported as `differs on both sides,
…` and not counted as a conflict; the run that ends with the sides agreeing
establishes the common state for the next one.

`sync` never deletes anything, on either side: a file deleted locally since
the last run comes back from the server (`missing locally`), a blob deleted on
the server is re-uploaded from the local copy (`missing on server`), a key
gone from both sides is simply forgotten. Propagating deletions is not part
of the spec. Transfers are the same as `push`'s and `pull`'s (streamed `PUT`
with the returned hash checked, staged `GET` renamed into place only when the
hash matches the listing), with one progress line per transfer in key order
and a summary; the exit code is `0` when the run completed.

The state lives inside `<dir>` because that is the only thing the client
container can see between runs. `.syncbox/` at the top of `<dir>` is
reserved for it: the scan never descends into it (so `push`, `status` and
`sync` never upload it) and a key under it is refused like an unsafe key (so
no download can write into it). Entries are kept per server URL, so a
directory may be synced with several servers; the file is rewritten
atomically (staging file + `rename`) and also after a failed run, for the
keys that were already reconciled, so a rerun continues where the failed one
stopped. A corrupt or newer-versioned state file is reported with its path
before anything is transferred; deleting it resets the common state, after
which the next run uses the no-common-state rules above. `.syncbox/` is also
excluded when `<dir>` is mounted read-only (`push`, `status`), which simply
means those commands never write it.

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` failure (server unreachable, server answered
outside the contract, unreadable file, file name that is not valid UTF-8 and
so cannot be a key, SHA-256 mismatch after a transfer, something in the way
of a file to be written, disk error while writing, unreadable or corrupt sync
state, a conflict whose server `modified_at` is not a timestamp), `2` usage
error. In this
version a failure stops the command at the first problem with a clear
message; continuing past per-file failures and reporting them at the end is
ticket 11.

Inside the container `<dir>` is bind-mounted at `/work` — read-only for
`push` and `status`, read-write for `pull` and `sync` (`run-client` picks the
mode per command through `SYNCBOX_DIR_MODE`) — and the container uses the
host network, so a `--server` URL that is valid for the caller
(`http://127.0.0.1:8080`, `http://localhost:8080`, a LAN address) is valid
inside the container too — nothing is rewritten. The container runs as the
caller's uid/gid, so it reads files with the caller's permissions and the
files `pull` creates belong to the caller.

Blobs are stored as plain files under `<data-dir>/blobs/<key>`; `<data-dir>/tmp/`
is the staging area for writes in progress (see “Atomic writes”). The listing
is derived from the files themselves on every request (no metadata index):
`key` is the path relative to `<data-dir>/blobs/`, and `size`, `sha256` and
`modified_at` are all read from one open file, so each entry describes a
single version even while the key is being replaced. Blobs placed into that
directory by other means are therefore listed too; directories, in-progress
staging files and names that are not valid UTF-8 are skipped.

Directories under `<data-dir>/blobs/` exist only while they hold a blob: `PUT`
creates them on demand and `DELETE` removes the ones it leaves empty (the root
itself stays). A key freed by `DELETE` therefore behaves exactly like one that
never existed — e.g. after deleting `docs/readme.txt` a `PUT` to `docs` is
accepted. Only regular files are blobs: `DELETE` of a key that names a
directory answers `404` and leaves its contents alone.

## Key validation

A `key` is a POSIX path relative to `<data-dir>/blobs/`. Every method on
`/blobs/{key}` (`GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT`, `DELETE`) runs the decoded key through
two independent checks before touching a file, and answers `400` (JSON
`{"error":"invalid key","detail":...}`) if either fails:

1. **Lexical** (`BlobStore#validate_key`): the key must be non-empty, valid
   UTF-8, free of NUL bytes, relative (no leading `/`), with no empty, `.` or
   `..` segments and no segment over 255 bytes. Overlong UTF-8 encodings and
   surrogate halves are invalid UTF-8 and therefore rejected too.
2. **On disk** (`BlobStore#path_for`): the longest existing prefix of the
   resulting path is resolved with `realpath(3)` (every symlink followed) and
   the location must lie *strictly inside* the resolved storage root. This is
   what keeps a well-formed key from escaping through a symlink that someone
   placed under `blobs/` — a link leading outside the root (or to the root
   itself) answers `400` for all methods, is left untouched, and is skipped
   by the listing. Symlinks that stay inside the root work like any other
   entry; the listing does not descend into symlinked directories.

The path is percent-decoded exactly once, so `%252e%252e` is the ordinary
directory name `%2e%2e`, not `..`; `..` inside a segment (`a..b`, `...`) is an
ordinary name as well. Nothing is created on disk for a rejected key, and a
rejected or malformed key never produces a 5xx.

## Atomic writes

`PUT` never writes to the target file. The body is streamed into a freshly
created staging file `<data-dir>/tmp/put-<32 hex digits>`, flushed and
`fsync`ed, and only then `rename(2)`d onto `<data-dir>/blobs/<key>`. Since
`rename(2)` swaps the directory entry atomically, a `GET` started at any
moment sees either the previous complete blob or the new complete one, never
a partially written file; a reader that already has the old file open reads
it to the end even though its directory entry is gone. The server does not
hold any locks: concurrent `PUT`s to the same key each stage into their own
randomly named file, the last `rename` wins and the other versions are
unlinked whole, and `PUT`s to different keys share nothing but the staging
directory. `modified_at` in the `PUT` response is the staged file's mtime,
which `rename` preserves.

`rename(2)` is only atomic within one filesystem, so the staging directory is
a sibling of the storage root inside the same data dir rather than the system
temp dir. This is verified, not assumed: at boot and on every `PUT` the server
checks that `blobs/` and `tmp/` report the same device, and refuses (exit 1 at
boot, `500` on `PUT`, nothing written) instead of falling back to a copy if
someone mounts them on different filesystems.

Staging files never outlive the request: on success the file has been renamed
away, and on any failure (rejected key, I/O error, client disconnect) it is
unlinked before the response. At boot the server removes `put-*` files a
previous process may have left behind by dying mid-write and reports the count
on stderr — safe because one server process owns a data dir, which is also
why no cross-process lock file is needed. `tmp/` lies outside the storage
root, so a staging file is never listed and cannot be reached through any
key (`../tmp/...` is rejected lexically, a symlink into `tmp/` by the
`realpath` check).

## Tests

```

The suite covers the write path deterministically (a probing request body

up under the key) and stochastically (writer, reader and listing threads on
one key, both in-process and through the real Puma server). Aborted uploads

   148	      # Sends the request built by the block and returns the response. The
   149	      # block returns a request, [request, io_to_close] or
   150	      # [request, io_to_close, on_response]; +on_response+ is called with the
   151	      # response while its body is still on the wire, so it can stream the
   152	      # body (a body it does not read is drained afterwards). Network failures
   153	      # become Unreachable; a failure on a connection that already served a
   154	      # request is retried once on a fresh connection, since the server may
   155	      # simply have closed an idle keep-alive connection. The block is called
   156	      # again for the retry, so each attempt starts from scratch.
   157	      def request(path)
   158	        attempts = 0
   159	        loop do
   160	          attempts += 1
   161	          reused = @requests_on_connection.positive?
   162	          # Outside the rescue below: a local failure while building the
   163	          # request (e.g. the file vanished) is not a network problem.
   164	          req, io, on_response = yield
   165	          begin
   166	            response = http.request(req) { |res| on_response&.call(res) }
   167	            @requests_on_connection += 1
   168	            return response
   169	          rescue *NETWORK_ERRORS => e
   170	            close
   171	            next if reused && attempts == 1
   172	
   173	            raise Unreachable, "cannot reach server at #{@base_url}: #{e.message} (#{req.method} #{path})"
   174	          rescue Error

   176	            # unread: the connection is not reusable, drop it.
   177	            close
   178	            raise

   183	              io&.close
   184	            rescue IOError, SystemCallError

   186	            end
   187	          end
   188	        end
   189	      end

   191	      def http

   194	        http = Net::HTTP.new(@base_url.host, @base_url.port)

   204	        http.ignore_eof = false

   210	      # Streams the body of a 200 response into +file+, hashing it. Only the
   211	      # file operations are wrapped: a socket failure raised by read_body must
   212	      # stay a network error (see NETWORK_ERRORS), a disk failure must not.
   213	      def receive_body(key, response, file, path)

   215	        size = 0
   216	        response.read_body do |chunk|
   217	          write_chunk(file, chunk, path)
   218	          digest << chunk
   219	          size += chunk.bytesize

   222	          file.flush
   223	          file.fsync

   225	          raise WriteError, "cannot write #{path}: #{e.message}"
   226	        end
   227	        GetResult.new(key: key, size: size, sha256: digest.hexdigest)
   228	      end
   229	
   230	      def write_chunk(file, chunk, path)
   231	        file.write(chunk)
   232	      rescue SystemCallError, IOError => e
   233	        raise WriteError, "cannot write #{path}: #{e.message}"
   234	      end

   240	        data.map do |item|
   241	          unless item.is_a?(Hash) && item["key"].is_a?(String) && item["sha256"].to_s.match?(SHA256_HEX)
   242	            raise ProtocolError, "GET #{path}: malformed list entry #{item.inspect[0, 200]}"
   243	          end
   244	
   245	          RemoteBlob.new(key: item["key"], size: item["size"], sha256: item["sha256"], modified_at: item["modified_at"])
   246	        end.sort_by(&:key)
   247	      end

   249	      def parse_put(path, body)
   250	        data = parse_json(path, body)
   251	        unless data.is_a?(Hash) && data["key"].is_a?(String) && data["sha256"].to_s.match?(SHA256_HEX)

   253	        end

   255	        PutResult.new(key: data["key"], size: data["size"], sha256: data["sha256"])

   258	      def parse_json(path, body)
   259	        JSON.parse(body.to_s)
   260	      rescue JSON::ParserError => e
   261	        raise ProtocolError, "#{path}: response is not valid JSON (#{e.message[0, 100]})"
   262	      end
   263	    end
   264	  end

     9	    # The local side of a sync: maps keys to paths inside one directory and
    10	    # hashes files.
    11	    #
    12	    # #scan walks the directory recursively: every regular file becomes a
    13	    # LocalFile whose key is its POSIX path relative to the directory (the
    14	    # same convention the server uses) and whose sha256 is the hex digest of
    15	    # its contents. Symlinks (to files or directories) and special files
    16	    # (sockets, FIFOs, devices) cannot be represented as blobs and are
    17	    # skipped with a warning — symlinks are never followed, so a link cannot
    18	    # drag anything from outside the directory into the upload or create a
    19	    # cycle. Hidden entries are ordinary files and are included. A name that
    20	    # is not valid UTF-8 cannot be a key (the server rejects it) and raises
    21	    # Error.
    22	    #
    23	    # #lookup / #path_for go the other way, from a key (as listed by the
    24	    # server) to the local path it stands for, with the same rule applied in
    25	    # reverse: a key never resolves through a symlink, and a key that could
    26	    # leave the directory is refused.
    27	    #
    28	    # The top-level entry STATE_DIR (".syncbox") is reserved for the client's
    29	    # own bookkeeping (see SyncState): the scan never descends into it, and a
    30	    # key under it is refused, so it is neither uploaded nor written to by a
    31	    # download.

    33	      class Error < StandardError; end
    34	
    35	      CHUNK_SIZE = 64 * 1024
    36	      STATE_DIR = ".syncbox"
    37	
    38	      # +mtime+ is the file's modification time, read when it was hashed.
    39	      LocalFile = Struct.new(:key, :path, :size, :sha256, :mode, :mtime, keyword_init: true)
    40	
    41	      # True if +key+ is, or lies under, the reserved STATE_DIR entry.
    42	      def self.reserved?(key)
    43	        key == STATE_DIR || key.start_with?("#{STATE_DIR}/")
    44	      end
    45	
    46	      # Yields a warning message for every skipped entry; returns the files
    47	      # sorted by key.

    52	      attr_reader :root
    53	
    54	      def initialize(dir)

    57	      end
    58	
    59	      def scan
    60	        require_directory!

    62	        files = []
    63	        Find.find(@root) do |path|
    64	          next if path == @root
    65	
    66	          key = key_for(path)
    67	          Find.prune if key == STATE_DIR # the client's own state, never a blob

    72	          elsif stat.directory?
    73	            next
    74	          elsif stat.file?
    75	            files << file_entry(key, path)
    76	          elsif block_given?
    77	            yield "skipping #{key}: not a regular file (#{stat.ftype})"
    78	          end

    83	      end

    85	      def require_directory!
    86	        raise Error, "not a directory: #{@root}" unless File.directory?(@root)
    87	      end

    89	      # The LocalFile currently stored under +key+, or nil if there is none.
    90	      # Anything other than a regular file at that path (a directory, a
    91	      # symlink — never followed —, a socket) is an Error: the key cannot be
    92	      # compared with, or written over, such an entry.

   106	      # The absolute path a key stands for. Keys come from the server and are
   107	      # not trusted: one that is absolute, contains "." or ".." segments,
   108	      # empty segments or NUL bytes is refused rather than resolved. Every

   122	      def validate_key(key)
   123	        utf8 = key.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
   124	        raise Error, "refusing key #{key.inspect} from the server: not valid UTF-8" unless utf8.valid_encoding?
   125	        raise Error, "refusing key #{key.inspect} from the server: contains a NUL byte" if key.include?("\0")
   126	        raise Error, "refusing key #{key.inspect} from the server: absolute path" if key.start_with?("/")
   127	
   128	        segments = key.split("/", -1)
   129	        if segments.empty? || segments.any?(&:empty?)
   130	          raise Error, "refusing key #{key.inspect} from the server: empty path segment"
   131	        end
   132	        if segments.any? { |s| s == "." || s == ".." }
   133	          raise Error, "refusing key #{key.inspect} from the server: contains a . or .. segment"
   134	        end
   135	        if self.class.reserved?(key)
   136	          raise Error, "refusing key #{key.inspect} from the server: #{STATE_DIR} is reserved for syncbox's own state"
   137	        end
   138	      end
   139	
   140	      # Checks every directory between the root and +dir+ (inclusive), from
   141	      # the top down, stopping at the first one that does not exist yet (its
   142	      # descendants cannot exist either). Verified directories are remembered
   143	      # for the lifetime of this tree, so a pull checks each one once.
   144	      def verify_ancestors(dir, key)
   145	        chain = []
   146	        current = dir
   147	        while current != @root && !@verified_dirs.include?(current)
   148	          chain.unshift(current)
   149	          current = File.dirname(current)
   150	        end
   151	
   152	        chain.each do |candidate|
   153	          stat = begin
   154	            File.lstat(candidate)
   155	          rescue Errno::ENOENT
   156	            return # does not exist yet: it will be created, nothing to verify
   157	          end
   158	          if stat.symlink?
   159	            raise Error, "#{key}: a symbolic link is in the way (#{relative(candidate)}); links are not followed"
   160	          elsif !stat.directory?
   161	            raise Error, "#{key}: #{relative(candidate)} is in the way and is not a directory"
   162	          end
   163	          @verified_dirs << candidate
   164	        end
   165	      rescue SystemCallError => e
   166	        raise Error, "#{key}: #{e.message}"
   167	      end
   168	
   169	      def relative(path)
   170	        path.byteslice((@root.bytesize + 1)..).to_s
   171	      end
   172	
   173	      def key_for(path)
   174	        key = path.byteslice((@root.bytesize + 1)..).dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
   175	        raise Error, "file name is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be a key: #{key.inspect}" unless key.valid_encoding?
   176	
   177	        key
   178	      end
   179	
   180	      def file_entry(key, path)
   181	        digest = Digest::SHA256.new
   182	        size = 0
   183	        mode = nil
   184	        mtime = nil
   185	        File.open(path, "rb") do |file|
   186	          stat = file.stat
   187	          mode = stat.mode & 0o7777
   188	          mtime = stat.mtime

   191	            size += chunk.bytesize
   192	          end
   193	        end

   195	      rescue SystemCallError => e
   196	        raise Error, "cannot read #{key}: #{e.message}"
   197	      end
   198	    end
   199	  end

    15	    # Pure: no filesystem or network access, so it is trivially unit-testable.
    16	    # Whether <dir> exists is checked by the command that uses it.
    17	    class Options
    18	      COMMANDS = %w[push pull sync status].freeze

    20	
    21	      class Error < StandardError; end

    27	
    28	      # +server+ is a URI::HTTP(S) without trailing slash in its path, so that
    29	      # "#{server}/blobs" is always well-formed.
    30	      def initialize(command:, dir:, server:)
    31	        @command = command
    32	        @dir = dir
    33	        @server = server
    34	      end
    35	
    36	      def self.parse(argv, env: ENV, program_name: "syncbox")
    37	        options = {}
    38	        parser = build_parser(options, program_name)
    39	
    40	        begin
    41	          positional = parser.parse(argv.dup)
    42	        rescue OptionParser::ParseError => e
    43	          raise Error, e.message
    44	        end
    45	
    46	        raise HelpRequested, parser.to_s if options[:help]
    47	
    48	        command, dir, *extra = positional
    49	        raise Error, "missing command (one of: #{COMMANDS.join(', ')})" if command.nil?
    50	        raise Error, "unknown command #{command.inspect} (expected one of: #{COMMANDS.join(', ')})" unless COMMANDS.include?(command)
    51	        raise Error, "missing <dir> argument" if dir.nil?
    52	        raise Error, "unexpected argument(s): #{extra.join(' ')}" unless extra.empty?
    53	
    54	        server = first_present(options[:server], env["SYNCBOX_SERVER"])
    55	        raise Error, "--server is required (or set SYNCBOX_SERVER)" if server.nil?
    56	
    57	        new(command: command, dir: dir, server: parse_server(server))
    58	      end

    62	      end

    65	        OptionParser.new do |o|
    66	          o.program_name = program_name
    67	          o.banner = "Usage: #{program_name} <#{COMMANDS.join('|')}> <dir> --server <url>"
    68	          o.separator ""
    69	          o.separator "Commands:"
    70	          o.separator "  push     Upload files that are missing on the server or differ from it (by SHA-256)"
    71	          o.separator "  pull     Download files that are missing locally or differ from the server (by SHA-256)"
    72	          o.separator "  sync     Both ways: upload local-only/changed files, download server-only/changed blobs;"
    73	          o.separator "           a file changed on both sides since the last sync goes to the fresher mtime, local on a tie"
    74	          o.separator "  status   Dry run: show what push and pull would do, changing nothing on either side"
    75	          o.separator ""
    76	          o.separator "Options:"
    77	          o.on("--server URL", "Base URL of the Syncbox server (required; env SYNCBOX_SERVER)") do |v|
    78	            options[:server] = v
    79	          end

    90	      # Accepts http(s)://host[:port][/prefix]; the path is kept (minus any

    95	        rescue URI::InvalidURIError => e

    97	        end

    99	        unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && SCHEMES.include?(uri.scheme) && uri.host && !uri.host.empty?
   100	          raise Error, "invalid server URL #{raw.inspect}: expected http://host[:port] or https://host[:port]"
   101	        end
   102	        raise Error, "invalid server URL #{raw.inspect}: query and fragment are not allowed" if uri.query || uri.fragment

   104	        uri.path = uri.path.sub(%r{/+\z}, "")

   106	      end

   109	  end

     5	    # `syncbox pull <dir>`: fetches the server's listing once and downloads
     6	    # every blob that is missing locally or whose SHA-256 differs from the
     7	    # local file's, writing it under <dir> at the path equal to its key

    13	    # renamed over it only after the bytes received hash to the sha256 the
    14	    # listing promised (see Transfer), so a target is either untouched or
    15	    # complete, never half-written. Failures stop the pull at the first
    16	    # problem with a clear message (continuing past per-file failures and
    17	    # reporting them is ticket 11).

     3	require "fileutils"
     4	require "securerandom"
     5	
     6	module Syncbox
     7	  module Client
     8	    # The two transfers every command is made of, shared by push, pull and
     9	    # sync: #upload streams a local file to the server with PUT /blobs/{key}
    10	    # and checks the sha256 the server reports back; #download fetches a blob
    11	    # with GET /blobs/{key} into a staging file next to its target and renames
    12	    # it into place once the bytes received hash to what the listing promised,
    13	    # so a local file is either untouched or complete, never half-written.
    14	    # Both print one progress line to +out+.
    15	    class Transfer
    16	      class Error < StandardError; end
    17	
    18	      STAGING_PREFIX = ".syncbox-tmp-"
    19	
    20	      def initialize(api:, out: $stdout, err: $stderr)
    21	        @api = api
    22	        @out = out
    23	        @err = err
    24	      end
    25	
    26	      # Uploads +file+ (a LocalTree::LocalFile); +reason+ is shown in the
    27	      # progress line. Returns the server's Api::PutResult.
    28	      def upload(file, reason)
    29	        result = @api.put(file.key, file.path)
    30	        if result.sha256 != file.sha256
    31	          raise Error, "#{file.key}: server stored sha256 #{result.sha256}, expected #{file.sha256} " \
    32	                       "(was the file modified during the upload?)"
    33	        end
    34	
    35	        @out.puts "uploaded #{file.key} (#{reason}, #{file.size} bytes)"
    36	        result
    37	      end
    38	
    39	      # Downloads +blob+ (an Api::RemoteBlob) to the path its key stands for
    40	      # in +tree+, replacing +local+ (the LocalTree::LocalFile currently there,
    41	      # or nil) while keeping its permission bits. Returns the Api::GetResult.
    42	      def download(tree, blob, local, reason)
    43	        target = tree.path_for(blob.key)
    44	        staging = nil
    45	        begin
    46	          FileUtils.mkdir_p(File.dirname(target))
    47	          staging = File.join(File.dirname(target), "#{STAGING_PREFIX}#{SecureRandom.hex(8)}")
    48	          result = @api.get(blob.key, staging)
    49	          verify(blob, result)
    50	          # Replacing a file keeps its permission bits (an executable stays
    51	          # executable); a new file gets the default ones.
    52	          File.chmod(local.mode, staging) if local&.mode
    53	          File.rename(staging, target)
    54	        rescue SystemCallError => e
    55	          raise Error, "#{blob.key}: #{e.message}"
    56	        ensure
    57	          discard(staging) if staging
    58	        end
    59	
    60	        @out.puts "downloaded #{blob.key} (#{reason}, #{result.size} bytes)"
    61	        result
    62	      end
    63	
    64	      private
    65	
    66	      def verify(blob, result)
    67	        return if result.sha256 == blob.sha256
    68	
    69	        raise Error, "#{blob.key}: downloaded sha256 #{result.sha256}, expected #{blob.sha256} from the listing " \
    70	                     "(was the blob replaced on the server during the transfer, or the transfer corrupted?)"
    71	      end
    72	
    73	      # Removes a staging file unless it has already been renamed into place.
    74	      def discard(staging)
    75	        File.unlink(staging)
    76	      rescue Errno::ENOENT
    77	        nil
    78	      rescue SystemCallError => e
    79	        @err.puts "syncbox: warning: cannot remove staging file #{staging}: #{e.message}"
    80	      end
    81	    end
    82	  end
    83	end

    90	module Syncbox
    91	  module Client
    92	    # The local side of a sync: maps keys to paths inside one directory and
    93	    # hashes files.
    94	    #
    95	    # #scan walks the directory recursively: every regular file becomes a
    96	    # LocalFile whose key is its POSIX path relative to the directory (the
    97	    # same convention the server uses) and whose sha256 is the hex digest of
    98	    # its contents. Symlinks (to files or directories) and special files
    99	    # (sockets, FIFOs, devices) cannot be represented as blobs and are
   100	    # skipped with a warning — symlinks are never followed, so a link cannot
   101	    # drag anything from outside the directory into the upload or create a
   102	    # cycle. Hidden entries are ordinary files and are included. A name that
   103	    # is not valid UTF-8 cannot be a key (the server rejects it) and raises
   104	    # Error.
   105	    #
   106	    # #lookup / #path_for go the other way, from a key (as listed by the
   107	    # server) to the local path it stands for, with the same rule applied in
   108	    # reverse: a key never resolves through a symlink, and a key that could
   109	    # leave the directory is refused.
   110	    #
   111	    # The top-level entry STATE_DIR (".syncbox") is reserved for the client's
   112	    # own bookkeeping (see SyncState): the scan never descends into it, and a
   113	    # key under it is refused, so it is neither uploaded nor written to by a
   114	    # download.
   115	    class LocalTree
   116	      class Error < StandardError; end
   117	
   118	      CHUNK_SIZE = 64 * 1024
   119	      STATE_DIR = ".syncbox"
   120	
   121	      # +mtime+ is the file's modification time, read when it was hashed.
   122	      LocalFile = Struct.new(:key, :path, :size, :sha256, :mode, :mtime, keyword_init: true)
   123	
   124	      # True if +key+ is, or lies under, the reserved STATE_DIR entry.
   125	      def self.reserved?(key)
   126	        key == STATE_DIR || key.start_with?("#{STATE_DIR}/")
   127	      end
   128	
   129	      # Yields a warning message for every skipped entry; returns the files
   130	      # sorted by key.
   131	      def self.scan(dir, &on_warning)
   132	        new(dir).scan(&on_warning)
   133	      end
   134	
   135	      attr_reader :root
   136	
   137	      def initialize(dir)
   138	        @root = File.expand_path(dir)
   139	        @verified_dirs = Set.new
   140	      end
   141	
   142	      def scan
   143	        require_directory!
   144	
   145	        files = []
   146	        Find.find(@root) do |path|
   147	          next if path == @root
   148	
   149	          key = key_for(path)
   150	          Find.prune if key == STATE_DIR # the client's own state, never a blob
   151	
   152	          stat = File.lstat(path)
   153	          if stat.symlink?
   154	            yield "skipping #{key}: symbolic links are not uploaded" if block_given?
   155	          elsif stat.directory?
   156	            next
   157	          elsif stat.file?
   158	            files << file_entry(key, path)
   159	          elsif block_given?
   160	            yield "skipping #{key}: not a regular file (#{stat.ftype})"
   161	          end
   162	        end
   163	        files.sort_by!(&:key)
   164	      rescue SystemCallError => e
   165	        raise Error, "cannot read #{@root}: #{e.message}"
   166	      end
   167	
   168	      def require_directory!
   169	        raise Error, "not a directory: #{@root}" unless File.directory?(@root)

   135	  module Client
   136	    # `syncbox sync <dir>`: push and pull in one pass, plus a conflict rule.
   137	    # Scans the directory, fetches the server's listing once and walks the
   138	    # union of keys; for each key the two sides and the last known common
   139	    # version (SyncState, kept in <dir>/.syncbox/state.json) decide what
   140	    # happens:
   141	    #
   142	    #   identical on both sides         nothing (the common version is noted)
   143	    #   only local                      upload   (as push would)
   144	    #   only on the server              download (as pull would)
   145	    #   differs, server == last common  only the local side changed: upload
   146	    #   differs, local  == last common  only the server changed: download
   147	    #   differs, both moved away from   conflict — the spec's rule, verbatim:
   148	    #   the last common version         the fresher of the server's
   149	    #                                   modified_at and the local mtime wins;
   150	    #                                   on a tie the local version wins
   151	    #   differs, no common version      no run has seen this key in sync yet,
   152	    #   known (first run)               so neither side can be told to be the
   153	    #                                   unchanged one; the same mtime rule
   154	    #                                   picks the side to copy
   155	    #
   156	    # "Differs" always means "the SHA-256 hashes differ"; mtimes are never
   157	    # consulted when the content is the same. The server's modified_at is the
   158	    # time the blob was stored (ISO 8601 UTC, millisecond precision), the
   159	    # local mtime comes from the filesystem; they are compared as instants.
   160	    #
   161	    # sync never deletes anything, on either side: a file that disappeared
   162	    # from one side since the last run is copied back from the other, exactly
   163	    # like a file that is only on one side for any other reason. Deletion
   164	    # propagation is not part of the spec.
   165	    #
   166	    # Transfers use Transfer (streamed PUT with sha256 check, staged GET with
   167	    # rename into place). The state is saved on the way out — also after a
   168	    # failure, for the keys that were already reconciled — so a rerun picks
   169	    # up where this run stopped. Failures stop the sync at the first problem
   170	    # with a clear message (continuing past per-file failures and reporting
   171	    # them is ticket 11).
   172	    class Sync
   173	      class Error < StandardError; end
   174	
   175	      Summary = Struct.new(:uploaded, :downloaded, :unchanged, :conflicts, keyword_init: true) do
   176	        def to_s
   177	          "sync done: #{uploaded} uploaded, #{downloaded} downloaded, #{unchanged} unchanged, " \
   178	            "#{conflicts} conflict(s) resolved"
   179	        end
   180	      end
   181	
   182	      # +server+ is the server URL as a string; it keys the base state, so
   183	      # one directory can be synced with more than one server.

   186	        @api = api
   187	        @server = server.to_s
   188	        @out = out
   189	        @err = err
   190	      end
   191	
   192	      def call
   193	        @tree = LocalTree.new(@dir)

   195	        @state = SyncState.load(@dir, server: @server)
   196	        local = @tree.scan { |warning| @err.puts "syncbox: warning: #{warning}" }.to_h { |f| [f.key, f] }

   199	        @summary = Summary.new(uploaded: 0, downloaded: 0, unchanged: 0, conflicts: 0)

   202	          # A key gone from both sides has no common version any more.
   203	          @state.keys.each { |key| @state.forget(key) unless local.key?(key) || remote.key?(key) }

   205	          (local.keys | remote.keys).sort.each { |key| reconcile(key, local[key], remote[key]) }

   208	          save_state(failing: !$!.nil?)
   209	        end

   215	      end

   227	          elsif file.sha256 == base

   230	            resolve_conflict(file, blob, base)
   231	          end
   232	        elsif file
   233	          upload(file, base ? "missing on server" : "new")
   234	        else
   235	          download(blob, nil, base ? "missing locally" : "new")
   236	        end
   237	      end
   238	
   239	      # Both sides differ from each other and neither is the last common
   240	      # version (or none is known): the fresher side wins, local on a tie.
   241	      def resolve_conflict(file, blob, base)
   242	        server_time = parse_modified_at(blob)
   243	        what = base ? "conflict" : "differs on both sides"
   244	        @summary.conflicts += 1 if base
   245	
   246	        if server_time > file.mtime
   247	          download(blob, file, "#{what}, server is newer")
   248	        elsif server_time == file.mtime
   249	          upload(file, "#{what}, same mtime, local wins")
   250	        else
   251	          upload(file, "#{what}, local is newer")
   252	        end
   253	      end
   254	
   255	      def upload(file, reason)
   256	        @transfer.upload(file, reason)
   257	        @state.record(file.key, file.sha256)
   258	        @summary.uploaded += 1
   259	      end
   260	
   261	      def download(blob, local, reason)
   262	        @transfer.download(@tree, blob, local, reason)
   263	        @state.record(blob.key, blob.sha256)
   264	        @summary.downloaded += 1
   265	      end

   269	      rescue ArgumentError

   271	                     "#{blob.modified_at.inspect} is not an ISO 8601 timestamp"
   272	      end

   274	      # Saves the state. While another error is already propagating, a
   275	      # failure to save is only a warning, so the original error is the one
   276	      # reported.
   277	      def save_state(failing:)
   278	        @state.save
   279	      rescue SyncState::Error => e
   280	        raise unless failing
   281	
   282	        @err.puts "syncbox: warning: #{e.message}"
   283	      end
   284	    end
   285	  end
   286	end

   289	require "json"
   290	require "securerandom"
   291	
   292	module Syncbox
   293	  module Client
   294	    # The "last known common state" that sync's conflict rule is defined
   295	    # against: for every key that was identical on both sides at the end of a
   296	    # sync run, the SHA-256 of that common version. On the next run a side
   297	    # whose hash still equals the recorded one has not changed, so a
   298	    # difference between the sides can be attributed to the other side alone;
   299	    # only when both sides have moved away from it is there a real conflict.
   300	    #
   301	    # Kept in <dir>/.syncbox/state.json, so it travels with the directory and
   302	    # survives between runs even though the client itself runs in a throwaway
   303	    # container that sees nothing but <dir>. The entry is reserved: LocalTree
   304	    # neither uploads it nor lets a download write into it. Entries are kept
   305	    # per server URL, so one directory can be synced with several servers
   306	    # without one sync confusing the other's base state.
   307	    #
   308	    #   {
   309	    #     "version": 1,
   310	    #     "servers": {
   311	    #       "http://127.0.0.1:8080": {
   312	    #         "files": { "docs/readme.txt": "<sha256 hex>", ... }
   313	    #       }
   314	    #     }
   315	    #   }
   316	    #
   317	    # #save rewrites the file atomically (staging file + rename), so a run
   318	    # interrupted while saving leaves the previous state, never a torn file.
   319	    class SyncState
   320	      class Error < StandardError; end
   321	
   322	      DIR = LocalTree::STATE_DIR
   323	      FILE = "state.json"
   324	      VERSION = 1
   325	      SHA256_HEX = /\A[0-9a-f]{64}\z/
   326	
   327	      attr_reader :path, :server
   328	
   329	      # Loads the state for +server+ (a URL string) kept under +dir+; a
   330	      # missing file is an empty state, anything unreadable or malformed is an
   331	      # Error naming the file (deleting it resets the base state; the next
   332	      # sync then falls back to the no-common-state rules).
   333	      def self.load(dir, server:)
   334	        path = File.join(File.expand_path(dir), DIR, FILE)
   335	        document = read_document(path)
   336	        files = document.dig("servers", server, "files") || {}
   337	        unless files.is_a?(Hash) && files.all? { |k, v| k.is_a?(String) && v.is_a?(String) && v.match?(SHA256_HEX) }
   338	          raise Error, "#{path}: malformed entry for server #{server}; delete the file to reset the sync state"
   339	        end
   340	
   341	        new(path, server, document, files.dup)
   342	      end
   343	
   344	      def self.read_document(path)
   345	        raw = File.read(path, mode: "rb")
   346	        document = JSON.parse(raw)
   347	        raise Error, "#{path}: expected a JSON object; delete the file to reset the sync state" unless document.is_a?(Hash)
   348	        unless document["version"] == VERSION
   349	          raise Error, "#{path}: unsupported sync state version #{document['version'].inspect} (this client writes " \
   350	                       "version #{VERSION}); delete the file to reset the sync state"
   351	        end
   352	        unless document["servers"].nil? || document["servers"].is_a?(Hash)
   353	          raise Error, "#{path}: \"servers\" must be an object; delete the file to reset the sync state"
   354	        end
   355	
   356	        document
   357	      rescue Errno::ENOENT
   358	        { "version" => VERSION, "servers" => {} }
   359	      rescue JSON::ParserError => e
   360	        raise Error, "#{path}: not valid JSON (#{e.message[0, 100]}); delete the file to reset the sync state"
   361	      rescue SystemCallError => e
   362	        raise Error, "cannot read sync state #{path}: #{e.message}"
   363	      end
   364	      private_class_method :read_document
   365	
   366	      def initialize(path, server, document, files)
   367	        @path = path
   368	        @server = server
   369	        @document = document
   370	        @files = files
   371	        @dirty = false
   372	      end
   373	
   374	      # SHA-256 of the last common version of +key+, or nil if none is known.
   375	      def [](key)
   376	        @files[key]
   377	      end
   378	
   379	      def key?(key)
   380	        @files.key?(key)
   381	      end
   382	
   383	      def keys
   384	        @files.keys
   385	      end
   386	
   387	      def empty?
   388	        @files.empty?
   389	      end
   390	
   391	      # Records +sha256+ as the common version of +key+.
   392	      def record(key, sha256)
   393	        return if @files[key] == sha256
   394	
   395	        @files[key] = sha256
   396	        @dirty = true
   397	      end
   398	
   399	      # Forgets +key+ (it is gone from both sides).
   400	      def forget(key)
   401	        @dirty = true if @files.delete(key)
   402	      end
   403	
   404	      def dirty?
   405	        @dirty
   406	      end
   407	
   408	      # Writes the state back if anything changed. Other servers' entries in
   409	      # the file are preserved as they were read.
   410	      def save
   411	        return unless @dirty
   412	
   413	        servers = (@document["servers"] || {}).dup
   414	        servers[@server] = { "files" => @files.sort.to_h }
   415	        document = { "version" => VERSION, "servers" => servers }
   416	
   417	        dir = File.dirname(@path)
   418	        staging = File.join(dir, ".#{FILE}.#{SecureRandom.hex(8)}.tmp")
   419	        begin
   420	          Dir.mkdir(dir) unless File.directory?(dir)
   421	          File.open(staging, File::WRONLY | File::CREAT | File::EXCL, 0o644, binmode: true) do |f|
   422	            f.write(JSON.pretty_generate(document), "\n")
   423	            f.flush
   424	            f.fsync
   425	          end
   426	          File.rename(staging, @path)
   427	        rescue SystemCallError => e
   428	          begin
   429	            File.unlink(staging)
   430	          rescue SystemCallError
   431	            nil
   432	          end
   433	          raise Error, "cannot write sync state #{@path}: #{e.message}"
   434	        end
   435	        @dirty = false
   436	        @path
   437	      end
   438	    end
   439	  end
   440	end

   144	    #   only on the server              download (as pull would)

   146	    #   differs, local  == last common  only the server changed: download

   149	    #                                   modified_at and the local mtime wins;

   153	    #                                   unchanged one; the same mtime rule
   154	    #                                   picks the side to copy

   158	    # time the blob was stored (ISO 8601 UTC, millisecond precision), the
   159	    # local mtime comes from the filesystem; they are compared as instants.

   161	    # sync never deletes anything, on either side: a file that disappeared

   289	require "json"
   290	require "securerandom"
   291	
   292	module Syncbox
   293	  module Client
   294	    # The "last known common state" that sync's conflict rule is defined
   295	    # against: for every key that was identical on both sides at the end of a
   296	    # sync run, the SHA-256 of that common version. On the next run a side
   297	    # whose hash still equals the recorded one has not changed, so a
   298	    # difference between the sides can be attributed to the other side alone;
   299	    # only when both sides have moved away from it is there a real conflict.
   300	    #
   301	    # Kept in <dir>/.syncbox/state.json, so it travels with the directory and
   302	    # survives between runs even though the client itself runs in a throwaway
   303	    # container that sees nothing but <dir>. The entry is reserved: LocalTree
   304	    # neither uploads it nor lets a download write into it. Entries are kept
   305	    # per server URL, so one directory can be synced with several servers
   306	    # without one sync confusing the other's base state.
   307	    #
   308	    #   {
   309	    #     "version": 1,
   310	    #     "servers": {
   311	    #       "http://127.0.0.1:8080": {
   312	    #         "files": { "docs/readme.txt": "<sha256 hex>", ... }
   313	    #       }
   314	    #     }
   315	    #   }
   316	    #
   317	    # #save rewrites the file atomically (staging file + rename), so a run
   318	    # interrupted while saving leaves the previous state, never a torn file.
   319	    class SyncState
   320	      class Error < StandardError; end
   321	
   322	      DIR = LocalTree::STATE_DIR
   323	      FILE = "state.json"
   324	      VERSION = 1
   325	      SHA256_HEX = /\A[0-9a-f]{64}\z/
   326	
   327	      attr_reader :path, :server
   328	
   329	      # Loads the state for +server+ (a URL string) kept under +dir+; a
   330	      # missing file is an empty state, anything unreadable or malformed is an
   331	      # Error naming the file (deleting it resets the base state; the next
   332	      # sync then falls back to the no-common-state rules).
   333	      def self.load(dir, server:)
   334	        path = File.join(File.expand_path(dir), DIR, FILE)
   335	        document = read_document(path)
   336	        files = document.dig("servers", server, "files") || {}
   337	        unless files.is_a?(Hash) && files.all? { |k, v| k.is_a?(String) && v.is_a?(String) && v.match?(SHA256_HEX) }
   338	          raise Error, "#{path}: malformed entry for server #{server}; delete the file to reset the sync state"
   339	        end
   340	
   341	        new(path, server, document, files.dup)
   342	      end
   343	
   344	      def self.read_document(path)
   345	        raw = File.read(path, mode: "rb")
   346	        document = JSON.parse(raw)
   347	        raise Error, "#{path}: expected a JSON object; delete the file to reset the sync state" unless document.is_a?(Hash)
   348	        unless document["version"] == VERSION
   349	          raise Error, "#{path}: unsupported sync state version #{document['version'].inspect} (this client writes " \
   350	                       "version #{VERSION}); delete the file to reset the sync state"
   351	        end
   352	        unless document["servers"].nil? || document["servers"].is_a?(Hash)
   353	          raise Error, "#{path}: \"servers\" must be an object; delete the file to reset the sync state"
   354	        end
   355	
   356	        document
   357	      rescue Errno::ENOENT
   358	        { "version" => VERSION, "servers" => {} }
   359	      rescue JSON::ParserError => e
   360	        raise Error, "#{path}: not valid JSON (#{e.message[0, 100]}); delete the file to reset the sync state"
   361	      rescue SystemCallError => e
   362	        raise Error, "cannot read sync state #{path}: #{e.message}"
   363	      end
   364	      private_class_method :read_document
   365	
   366	      def initialize(path, server, document, files)
   367	        @path = path
   368	        @server = server
   369	        @document = document
   370	        @files = files
   371	        @dirty = false
   372	      end
   373	
   374	      # SHA-256 of the last common version of +key+, or nil if none is known.
   375	      def [](key)
   376	        @files[key]
   377	      end
   378	
   379	      def key?(key)
   380	        @files.key?(key)
   381	      end
   382	
   383	      def keys
   384	        @files.keys
   385	      end
   386	
   387	      def empty?
   388	        @files.empty?
   389	      end

   392	      def record(key, sha256)

   395	        @files[key] = sha256
   396	        @dirty = true
   397	      end
   398	
   399	      # Forgets +key+ (it is gone from both sides).
   400	      def forget(key)

   402	      end
   403	
   404	      def dirty?
   405	        @dirty
   406	      end

   411	        return unless @dirty

   413	        servers = (@document["servers"] || {}).dup
   414	        servers[@server] = { "files" => @files.sort.to_h }

   432	          end

   434	        end
   435	        @dirty = false
   436	        @path
   437	      end
   438	    end
   439	  end
   440	end

     8	# Status against a scripted stand-in for the API: checks the comparison

    17	  # Only #list and #close exist. Anything that would change the server (PUT,
    18	  # DELETE) or fetch a body (GET /blobs/{key}) fails loudly: status has no
    19	  # business calling it.

    21	    attr_reader :list_calls, :closed

    23	    def initialize(remote)

    35	    end

    38	      raise "status must not PUT"
    39	    end

    42	      raise "status must not GET a blob"
    43	    end

    46	      raise "status must not DELETE"

10:## Running
16:# Upload raw bytes under a key (nested directories are created on demand),
17:# then download them back. Missing keys answer 404.
19:#   201  {"key":"docs/readme.txt","sha256":"<hex>","size":<bytes>}
21:#   200  application/octet-stream, the stored bytes
23:# List every stored blob with its metadata (sorted by key; [] when empty).
25:#   200  [{"key":"docs/readme.txt","size":<bytes>,"sha256":"<hex>",
26:#         "modified_at":"2026-10-06T03:36:49.366Z"}]
28:# Delete a blob: 204 with no body; afterwards GET answers 404 and the key is
29:# gone from the listing. Deleting a key that does not exist answers 404.
31:#   204
33:#   404  {"error":"not found"}
35:# Keys are validated on every /blobs/{key} method: ".." segments, absolute
36:# paths and names that cannot be a file on the server answer 400 with a JSON
37:# body — the request never reaches the filesystem. (--path-as-is stops curl
38:# from normalising the path client-side.)
40:#   400  {"error":"invalid key","detail":"key must not contain . or .. segments"}
42:#   400  {"error":"invalid key","detail":"key must be relative"}
44:#   400  {"error":"invalid key","detail":"key is not valid UTF-8"}

#   sync done: 2 uploaded, 2 downloaded, 58 unchanged, 1 conflict(s) resolved

SYNCBOX_SERVER=http://127.0.0.1:8080 ./run-client pull ./photos   # env instead of --server
```

`run-client <push|pull|sync|status> <dir> --server <url>` forwards the
subcommand and arguments to the `syncbox` executable (`bin/syncbox`) running
in a container; `--server` falls back to `SYNCBOX_SERVER`.

`push` walks `<dir>` recursively; a file's key is its POSIX path relative to
`<dir>` (`docs/readme.txt`), exactly the server's key convention, and is sent
percent-encoded so names with spaces or non-ASCII characters round-trip
byte for byte. Hidden files are included. Symbolic links (to files or
directories) and special files (sockets, FIFOs, devices) cannot be blobs and
are skipped with a warning on stderr — links are never followed. The server
listing (`GET /blobs`) is fetched once; each local file whose key is missing
there or whose `sha256` differs is streamed with `PUT /blobs/{key}`, and the
`sha256` the server reports back is checked against the local one. Progress
goes to stdout (one line per uploaded file plus a summary), warnings and
errors to stderr.

`pull` fetches the listing once and compares each blob's `sha256` with the
file at `<dir>/<key>`: a blob with no local file, or whose hash differs, is
fetched with `GET /blobs/{key}`; one with an identical local file is skipped
without a request. Each download is streamed into a staging file
(`.syncbox-tmp-<16 hex digits>`) in the target's directory, hashed on the
way, flushed to disk and `rename(2)`d onto `<dir>/<key>` only if the hash
matches the listing — so a file under `<dir>` is either untouched or
complete, never half-written, and a blob replaced on the server during the
pull (or a corrupted transfer) is reported instead of installed. Replacing a
file keeps its permission bits; a new file gets the default ones. Missing
parent directories are created. Staging files are removed on every outcome,
including an interrupted run (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM); only a hard kill can leave
one behind. Keys from the listing are not trusted: an absolute key, one with
`.` or `..` segments, empty segments or NUL bytes is refused, and a key is
never resolved through a symlink — a symlinked directory on the way, or a
directory, symlink or special file at the target itself, is reported as "in
the way" and nothing is written, mirroring `push`, which never follows links
either. Local files and directories the server does not list are never
deleted or modified; `pull` only adds and replaces.

`status` is the dry run of both: it scans `<dir>` like `push`, fetches the
listing once like `pull`, and compares the two by key and `sha256`. Every key
falls into exactly one group — `upload` (only local; `push` would upload it),
`download` (only on the server; `pull` would download it), `differs` (on both
sides with different content; `push` would upload the local version, `pull`
would download the server's — which one `sync` picks is decided by its
conflict rule, and `status` does not guess) or unchanged (identical, only
counted). Lines are grouped in that order and sorted by key, followed by a
summary line; an identical tree prints just the `in sync` summary. The
command never changes anything: no file under `<dir>` is created, modified
or removed, and the only request it sends is `GET /blobs` — the listing
already carries every hash the comparison needs, so not even `GET
/blobs/{key}` is issued, let alone `PUT` or `DELETE`. A download that `pull`
would refuse (a directory or symlink where the file would go, a key that
could leave the directory) is still listed as a download, with a `pull would
fail: …` note. The exit code is `0` whenever the comparison succeeded,
regardless of how many differences there are.

`sync` is `push` and `pull` in one pass plus the spec's conflict rule. It
scans `<dir>`, fetches the listing once and walks the union of keys. A key
present on one side only is copied to the other (`uploaded … (new, …)` /
`downloaded … (new, …)`); a key identical on both sides is left alone. When
the hashes differ, the *last known common state* decides whose change it is:
`sync` records, in `<dir>/.syncbox/state.json`, the SHA-256 of every key
that was identical on both sides at the end of a run. On the next run a side
whose hash still equals that recorded value has not changed, so the
difference belongs to the other side alone and is copied in that direction
(`changed locally` → upload, `changed on server` → download) — timestamps
play no role in these cases. Only when *both* sides have moved away from the
common version is it a conflict, resolved exactly as the spec says: the
fresher of the server's `modified_at` (the time the blob was stored, from
`GET /blobs`) and the local file's mtime wins, and on a tie the local version
wins (`conflict, server is newer` / `conflict, local is newer` /
`conflict, same mtime, local wins`). The two instants are compared exactly;
since `modified_at` has millisecond precision, a local mtime inside the same
millisecond but after it counts as newer, which gives the same answer as the
tie rule. Content is compared by hash only — a file touched but not changed
is unchanged. When no common version is known yet (the first run on a
directory, or a key never seen in sync before) and the two sides differ, the
same mtime rule picks the side to copy, reported as `differs on both sides,
…` and not counted as a conflict; the run that ends with the sides agreeing
establishes the common state for the next one.

`sync` never deletes anything, on either side: a file deleted locally since
the last run comes back from the server (`missing locally`), a blob deleted on
the server is re-uploaded from the local copy (`missing on server`), a key
gone from both sides is simply forgotten. Propagating deletions is not part
of the spec. Transfers are the same as `push`'s and `pull`'s (streamed `PUT`
with the returned hash checked, staged `GET` renamed into place only when the
hash matches the listing), with one progress line per transfer in key order
and a summary; the exit code is `0` when the run completed.

The state lives inside `<dir>` because that is the only thing the client
container can see between runs. `.syncbox/` at the top of `<dir>` is
reserved for it: the scan never descends into it (so `push`, `status` and
`sync` never upload it) and a key under it is refused like an unsafe key (so
no download can write into it). Entries are kept per server URL, so a
directory may be synced with several servers; the file is rewritten
atomically (staging file + `rename`) and also after a failed run, for the
keys that were already reconciled, so a rerun continues where the failed one
stopped. A corrupt or newer-versioned state file is reported with its path
before anything is transferred; deleting it resets the common state, after
which the next run uses the no-common-state rules above. `.syncbox/` is also
excluded when `<dir>` is mounted read-only (`push`, `status`), which simply
means those commands never write it.

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` failure (server unreachable, server answered
outside the contract, unreadable file, file name that is not valid UTF-8 and
so cannot be a key, SHA-256 mismatch after a transfer, something in the way
of a file to be written, disk error while writing, unreadable or corrupt sync
state, a conflict whose server `modified_at` is not a timestamp), `2` usage
error. In this
version a failure stops the command at the first problem with a clear
message; continuing past per-file failures and reporting them at the end is
ticket 11.

Inside the container `<dir>` is bind-mounted at `/work` — read-only for
`push` and `status`, read-write for `pull` and `sync` (`run-client` picks the
mode per command through `SYNCBOX_DIR_MODE`) — and the container uses the
host network, so a `--server` URL that is valid for the caller
(`http://127.0.0.1:8080`, `http://localhost:8080`, a LAN address) is valid
inside the container too — nothing is rewritten. The container runs as the
caller's uid/gid, so it reads files with the caller's permissions and the
files `pull` creates belong to the caller.

Blobs are stored as plain files under `<data-dir>/blobs/<key>`; `<data-dir>/tmp/`
is the staging area for writes in progress (see “Atomic writes”). The listing
is derived from the files themselves on every request (no metadata index):
`key` is the path relative to `<data-dir>/blobs/`, and `size`, `sha256` and
`modified_at` are all read from one open file, so each entry describes a
single version even while the key is being replaced. Blobs placed into that

`run-client <push|pull|sync|status> <dir> --server <url>` forwards the
subcommand and arguments to the `syncbox` executable (`bin/syncbox`) running
in a container; `--server` falls back to `SYNCBOX_SERVER`.

`push` walks `<dir>` recursively; a file's key is its POSIX path relative to
`<dir>` (`docs/readme.txt`), exactly the server's key convention, and is sent
percent-encoded so names with spaces or non-ASCII characters round-trip
byte for byte. Hidden files are included. Symbolic links (to files or
directories) and special files (sockets, FIFOs, devices) cannot be blobs and
are skipped with a warning on stderr — links are never followed. The server
listing (`GET /blobs`) is fetched once; each local file whose key is missing
there or whose `sha256` differs is streamed with `PUT /blobs/{key}`, and the
`sha256` the server reports back is checked against the local one. Progress
goes to stdout (one line per uploaded file plus a summary), warnings and
errors to stderr.

`pull` fetches the listing once and compares each blob's `sha256` with the
file at `<dir>/<key>`: a blob with no local file, or whose hash differs, is
fetched with `GET /blobs/{key}`; one with an identical local file is skipped
without a request. Each download is streamed into a staging file
(`.syncbox-tmp-<16 hex digits>`) in the target's directory, hashed on the
way, flushed to disk and `rename(2)`d onto `<dir>/<key>` only if the hash
matches the listing — so a file under `<dir>` is either untouched or
complete, never half-written, and a blob replaced on the server during the
pull (or a corrupted transfer) is reported instead of installed. Replacing a
file keeps its permission bits; a new file gets the default ones. Missing
parent directories are created. Staging files are removed on every outcome,
including an interrupted run (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM); only a hard kill can leave
one behind. Keys from the listing are not trusted: an absolute key, one with
`.` or `..` segments, empty segments or NUL bytes is refused, and a key is
never resolved through a symlink — a symlinked directory on the way, or a
directory, symlink or special file at the target itself, is reported as "in
the way" and nothing is written, mirroring `push`, which never follows links
either. Local files and directories the server does not list are never
deleted or modified; `pull` only adds and replaces.

`status` is the dry run of both: it scans `<dir>` like `push`, fetches the
listing once like `pull`, and compares the two by key and `sha256`. Every key
falls into exactly one group — `upload` (only local; `push` would upload it),
`download` (only on the server; `pull` would download it), `differs` (on both
sides with different content; `push` would upload the local version, `pull`
would download the server's — which one `sync` picks is decided by its
conflict rule, and `status` does not guess) or unchanged (identical, only
counted). Lines are grouped in that order and sorted by key, followed by a
summary line; an identical tree prints just the `in sync` summary. The
command never changes anything: no file under `<dir>` is created, modified
or removed, and the only request it sends is `GET /blobs` — the listing
already carries every hash the comparison needs, so not even `GET
/blobs/{key}` is issued, let alone `PUT` or `DELETE`. A download that `pull`
would refuse (a directory or symlink where the file would go, a key that
could leave the directory) is still listed as a download, with a `pull would
fail: …` note. The exit code is `0` whenever the comparison succeeded,
regardless of how many differences there are.

`sync` is `push` and `pull` in one pass plus the spec's conflict rule. It
scans `<dir>`, fetches the listing once and walks the union of keys. A key
present on one side only is copied to the other (`uploaded … (new, …)` /
`downloaded … (new, …)`); a key identical on both sides is left alone. When
the hashes differ, the *last known common state* decides whose change it is:
`sync` records, in `<dir>/.syncbox/state.json`, the SHA-256 of every key
that was identical on both sides at the end of a run. On the next run a side
whose hash still equals that recorded value has not changed, so the
difference belongs to the other side alone and is copied in that direction
(`changed locally` → upload, `changed on server` → download) — timestamps
play no role in these cases. Only when *both* sides have moved away from the
common version is it a conflict, resolved exactly as the spec says: the
fresher of the server's `modified_at` (the time the blob was stored, from
`GET /blobs`) and the local file's mtime wins, and on a tie the local version
wins (`conflict, server is newer` / `conflict, local is newer` /
`conflict, same mtime, local wins`). The two instants are compared exactly;
since `modified_at` has millisecond precision, a local mtime inside the same
millisecond but after it counts as newer, which gives the same answer as the
tie rule. Content is compared by hash only — a file touched but not changed

directory, or a key never seen in sync before) and the two sides differ, the
same mtime rule picks the side to copy, reported as `differs on both sides,
…` and not counted as a conflict; the run that ends with the sides agreeing
establishes the common state for the next one.

`sync` never deletes anything, on either side: a file deleted locally since
the last run comes back from the server (`missing locally`), a blob deleted on
the server is re-uploaded from the local copy (`missing on server`), a key
gone from both sides is simply forgotten. Propagating deletions is not part

hash matches the listing), with one progress line per transfer in key order

directory may be synced with several servers; the file is rewritten
atomically (staging file + `rename`) and also after a failed run, for the
keys that were already reconciled, so a rerun continues where the failed one
stopped. A corrupt or newer-versioned state file is reported with its path

  def test_pull_downloads_a_tree_then_only_what_changed_and_keeps_local_only_files
    with_tmpdir do |dir|
      src = File.join(dir, "src")
      dst = File.join(dir, "dst")
      write(src, "docs/readme.txt", "hello")
      write(src, "docs/img/logo.png", "\x89PNG".b)
      write(src, "sp ace/ü.txt", "")
      write(src, ".hidden", "h")
      big = Random.new(11).bytes(1_500_000)
      write(src, "big.bin", big)
      FileUtils.mkdir_p(dst)
      write(dst, "local-only.txt", "mine")
      write(dst, "docs/readme.txt", "stale")

      with_running_server(File.join(dir, "store")) do |port|
        url = "http://127.0.0.1:#{port}"
        _, stderr, status = run_client("push", src, "--server", url)
        assert_equal 0, status.exitstatus, stderr

        stdout, stderr, status = run_client("pull", dst, "--server", url)
        assert_equal 0, status.exitstatus, "stdout: #{stdout}\nstderr: #{stderr}"
        assert_equal "", stderr
        assert_equal <<~OUT, stdout
          downloaded .hidden (new, 1 bytes)
          downloaded big.bin (new, 1500000 bytes)
          downloaded docs/img/logo.png (new, 4 bytes)
          downloaded docs/readme.txt (changed, 5 bytes)
          downloaded sp ace/ü.txt (new, 0 bytes)
          pull done: 5 downloaded, 0 unchanged, 5 blob(s) listed
        OUT
        assert_equal local_hashes(src), local_hashes(dst).except("local-only.txt"), "pulled files must be byte-identical"
        assert_equal "mine", File.read(File.join(dst, "local-only.txt")), "pull leaves local-only files alone"
        assert_equal big, File.binread(File.join(dst, "big.bin"))

        # Nothing changed: nothing is downloaded, local mtimes stay.
        before = mtimes(dst)
        stdout, stderr, status = run_client("pull", dst, "--server", url)
        assert_equal 0, status.exitstatus, stderr
        assert_equal "pull done: 0 downloaded, 5 unchanged, 5 blob(s) listed\n", stdout
        assert_equal before, mtimes(dst), "identical files must not be rewritten"

        # One changed and one new on the server, one deleted on the server
        # (pull never deletes), one edited locally (pull restores the server's
        # version — it is "different", and pull has no notion of local wins).
        Net::HTTP.start("127.0.0.1", port) do |http|
          http.put("/blobs/docs/readme.txt", "hello world", "content-type" => "application/octet-stream")
          http.put("/blobs/new.txt", "n", "content-type" => "application/octet-stream")
          http.delete("/blobs/.hidden")
        end
        write(dst, "sp ace/ü.txt", "edited locally")
        stdout, _, status = run_client("pull", dst, "--server", url)
        assert_equal 0, status.exitstatus
        assert_equal <<~OUT, stdout
          downloaded docs/readme.txt (changed, 11 bytes)
          downloaded new.txt (new, 1 bytes)
          downloaded sp ace/ü.txt (changed, 0 bytes)
          pull done: 3 downloaded, 2 unchanged, 5 blob(s) listed
        OUT
        assert_equal "hello world", File.read(File.join(dst, "docs/readme.txt"))
        assert_equal "n", File.read(File.join(dst, "new.txt"))
        assert_equal "", File.read(File.join(dst, "sp ace/ü.txt"))
        assert_equal "h", File.read(File.join(dst, ".hidden")), "pull never deletes local files"
        assert_equal remote_hashes(port), local_hashes(dst).except("local-only.txt", ".hidden")
      end
    end
  end

  # A minimal HTTP/1.1 server that records every request it receives, answers
  # GET /blobs with a fixed listing and everything else with 500 — proof of
  # which requests a command sends, independent of the real server's state.
  class RecordingHttpServer
    attr_reader :port

    def self.open(listing)
      server = new(listing)
      yield server
    ensure
      server&.close
    end

    def initialize(listing)
      @body = JSON.generate(listing)
      @socket = TCPServer.new("127.0.0.1", 0)
      @port = @socket.addr[1]
      @requests = []
      @mutex = Mutex.new
      @acceptor = Thread.new { accept_loop }
    end

    def requests
      @mutex.synchronize { @requests.dup }
    end

    def close
      @socket.close
      @acceptor.join(5)
    end

    private

    def accept_loop
      loop do
        conn = @socket.accept
        Thread.new { serve(conn) }
      end
    rescue IOError, SystemCallError
      nil # socket closed
    end

    def serve(conn)
      while (request_line = conn.gets)
        method, path, = request_line.split(" ")
        headers = {}
        while (line = conn.gets) && line != "\r\n"
          name, value = line.split(":", 2)
          headers[name.downcase] = value.to_s.strip
        end
        conn.read(headers["content-length"].to_i) if headers["content-length"]
        @mutex.synchronize { @requests << [method, path] }
        if method == "GET" && path == "/blobs"
          respond(conn, "200 OK", "application/json", @body)
        else
          respond(conn, "500 Internal Server Error", "text/plain", "unexpected #{method} #{path}")
        end
      end
    rescue IOError, SystemCallError
      nil
    ensure
      conn.close
    end

    def respond(conn, status, type, body)
      conn.write "HTTP/1.1 #{status}\r\nContent-Type: #{type}\r\nContent-Length: #{body.bytesize}\r\n\r\n#{body}"
    end
  end

  private

  def run_client(*args, env: {}, chdir: nil)
    opts = chdir ? { chdir: chdir } : {}
    Open3.popen3(clean_env(env), CLIENT_BIN, *args, opts) do |stdin, stdout, stderr, wait_thr|
      stdin.close
      out_reader = Thread.new { stdout.read }
      err_reader = Thread.new { stderr.read }
      unless wait_thr.join(RUN_TIMEOUT)
        Process.kill("KILL", wait_thr.pid)
        flunk "#{CLIENT_BIN} #{args.join(' ')} did not exit within #{RUN_TIMEOUT}s"
      end
      [out_reader.value.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8), err_reader.value.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8), wait_thr.value]
    end
  end

  def put_blob(port, key, content)
    Net::HTTP.start("127.0.0.1", port) do |http|
      response = http.put("/blobs/#{Syncbox::Client::Api.encode_key(key)}", content, "content-type" => "application/octet-stream")
      assert_equal "201", response.code, response.body
    end
  end

  def remote_list(port)
    JSON.parse(Net::HTTP.get(URI("http://127.0.0.1:#{port}/blobs")))
  end

  def remote_hashes(port)
    remote_list(port).to_h { |m| [m["key"], m["sha256"]] }
  end

  def mtimes(dir)
    local_hashes(dir).keys.to_h { |rel| [rel, File.mtime(File.join(dir, rel))] }
  end

  # Every entry under +dir+ with its type, content hash and mtime — enough to
  # notice any creation, modification or removal.
  def snapshot(dir)
    Dir.glob("**/*", File::FNM_DOTMATCH, base: dir).sort.map do |rel|
      path = File.join(dir, rel)
      stat = File.lstat(path)
      [rel, stat.ftype, stat.file? ? Digest::SHA256.file(path).hexdigest : nil, stat.mtime]
    end
  end

  def local_hashes(dir)
    Dir.glob("**/*", File::FNM_DOTMATCH, base: dir)
       .select { |rel| File.file?(File.join(dir, rel)) }
       .to_h { |rel| [rel, Digest::SHA256.file(File.join(dir, rel)).hexdigest] }
  end

  def write(dir, rel, content)
    path = File.join(dir, rel)
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(File.dirname(path))
    File.binwrite(path, content)
  end
end
